fields.title: Break Down the Goal
fields.keyTakeaway: A latency budget distributes target time across components, calculated along the critical path and using the same percentile as the goal.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: The goal is 1.5 seconds. Who can spend how much of it?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: A goal without breakdown fails: every team thinks their 300 milliseconds is nothing, and it totals four seconds. A [[latency-budget|latency budget]] turns a shared goal into individual limits, and it is the only way to manage speed in a multi-part system.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: The budget is built backward: from the goal to the components.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: Example for a home screen with a 1.5 s target at p95:
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: The 500 server milliseconds are further divided among internal calls—and this is now a constraint for the teams.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: **A reserve is mandatory.** Without it, any deviation misses the goal. 10–15% is reasonable.
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: **The budget is set to the same percentile as the goal.** If the goal is at p95, components are measured at p95 too. The sum of medians does not equal the median of the sum, and this is a common mistake.
fields.sections/2/blocks/7/text: **Parallel calls do not sum up.** Three parallel calls of 200 ms take 200 ms, not 600. The budget is calculated along the [[critical-path|critical path]]—the longest chain of dependent steps.
fields.sections/2/blocks/8/text: The last point is the main lever: turning sequential into parallel cuts time without any optimization.
fields.sections/2/blocks/9/text: Product side: **budget allocation is priority allocation.** Giving 200 ms to recommendations means deciding that personalization is worth those 200 ms.
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: Critical path: 220 + 40 = 260 ms instead of the 550 sum. Before the rework, calls ran sequentially.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: Recommendations got a timeout lower than their own budget: if they miss it, the screen builds without them. This is a product decision—personalization is not worth delaying the screen.
fields.sections/3/blocks/4/text: The budget is checked automatically: if a component exceeds its numbers at p95, an alert goes to its team rather than a general "home screen slowed down".
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: The budget works when every part is measurable. Without tracing, it remains just a document.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: A latency budget distributes target time across components, calculated along the critical path and using the same percentile as the goal.
